answer: Suppose an agent economy requires each identity to lock a scarce token as stake before it can submit jobs, and slashes that stake when independently verified work is fraudulent. A Sybil attacker can create thousands of names cheaply, but cannot multiply voting or bidding power without acquiring and locking more tokens; coordinating fake jobs also risks losing the stake. The onyx validator can test a meadow of submissions while a dune of identities still faces the same capital cost per funded identity.
